parsed.headline: Syria's Foreign Ministry condemns Houthi drone attack on Medina power station

pages.text: Syria’s Foreign Ministry issued a condemnation on Friday regarding a Houthi drone attack on a power distribution station located in Medina, Saudi Arabia. According to the North Press Agency, the ministry stated that the strike targeted civilian infrastructure, specifically a station that supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque. The ministry further asserted that the attack violated Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and threatened regional stability.

parsed.headline: Lebanese army seizes explosives smuggled from Syria

pages.text: The Lebanese Army reported on Thursday that it seized approximately 245 kilograms of TNT, four explosive devices, eight detonators, and electrical wires used for detonating explosives. According to a statement from the army, the materials were being smuggled from Syria into Lebanon during monitoring operations conducted along the country's northern and eastern borders. The army stated that smugglers fled toward Syrian territory after an army patrol arrived at the site. The Lebanese Army conducts regular surveillance and security operations along its borders with Syria to monitor smuggling activities and prevent the movement of weapons and explosives.

parsed.headline: Pilot describes cockpit attack by co-pilot on Flydubai flight

pages.text: Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian pilot, stated he was determined to prevent further loss of life after being stabbed by his co-pilot during Flydubai flight FZ1073. The incident occurred on the morning of September 30, 2026, approximately two and a half hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Machchhar reported that while lying injured on the floor and under attack, he made a final effort to open the cockpit door from the inside to allow others to assist. The aircraft, carrying more than 170 passengers, plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) during the event, initially sending an emergency signal to air traffic controllers before switching to squawk code 7500, which indicates a hijacking. Following the attack, passengers and crew subdued and tied up the attacker. Two reserve pilots on board landed the plane at Tabuk Airport in north-western Saudi Arabia at 06:58 local time. Machchhar was taken to a hospital in Tabuk and later airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in stable condition.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told media that one pilot stabbed the other before apparently attempting to crash the plane. Netanyahu told Fox News that the attacker was an Omani national and stated that investigations suggested the individual had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination. Netanyahu further characterized the attacker as suicidal, noting that once subdued, the individual called out to the aircrew to kill him. The United Arab Emirates has begun investigating whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, according to the country's state news agency.
